title: badger/table: remove redundant block decode in iterator

source.license_note: Real upstream badger optimization PR #1512 (module v2); measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up table iteration by removing a redundant block decode/seek performed eagerly when a new Table iterator is constructed, without changing behavior.
task.instructions: Optimize the table package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkRandomRead measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: Table.NewIterator eagerly calls ti.next() during construction, decoding/seeking the first block before the caller has positioned the iterator, doing redundant work on every iterator created.

ops_fault.description: Constructing a table iterator eagerly advances to and decodes the first block via ti.next() in NewIterator, repeating work that the subsequent Seek/Rewind redoes on the hot read path in table/iterator.go.
detection_keywords: redundant block decode on iterator creation
block decoded before seek positions it
slow ns/op on random table reads
repair_keywords: defer first block decode to Seek/Rewind

visible_context.issue_text: Random reads through table iterators are slower than expected; every NewIterator call eagerly decodes the first block even though the caller seeks afterward, redoing the same decode work.
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization PR; the redundant eager decode removed from the constructor is the optimization under test.
